**Clinical Note Template**

**1. Patient Information**

Name: Arthur Miller
Age/Gender: 80 years/Male
Hospital Stay Dates: October 26, 2023 to November 15, 2023 (with multiple admissions/discharges)
Admitting Diagnosis:  Suspected colorectal cancer with bowel obstruction
Discharge Diagnosis: Stage II Colon Cancer, Partial bowel obstruction resolved, Anemia, Dehydration

**2. Visit Details**

**[October 26, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit: Acute abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation for 3 days.
Interventions:  Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), abdominal X-ray, CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis.
Findings/Results:  CBC showed anemia (Hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL), elevated white blood cell count (12,000/µL). CMP revealed mild dehydration. Abdominal X-ray showed dilated loops of bowel suggestive of obstruction. CT scan confirmed a large mass in the sigmoid colon causing partial bowel obstruction.
Treatment Plan:  Intravenous fluids (normal saline), bowel rest (NPO),  nasogastric tube placement for decompression,  pain management with morphine sulfate (IV).  Surgical consultation requested.


**[October 26, 2023, 21:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Evaluation of bowel obstruction.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of imaging studies.
Findings/Results:  Tenderness to palpation in the left lower quadrant.  Confirmed findings from the CT scan.
Treatment Plan:  Schedule for elective sigmoid colectomy the following morning.  Continue IV fluids and pain management.


**[October 27, 2023, 08:00]**

Provider Role: Anesthesiologist & Surgical Team
Reason for Visit:  Sigmoid colectomy.
Interventions:  Sigmoid colectomy with end-to-end anastomosis.
Findings/Results:  Procedure completed without significant complications.  Specimen sent for pathology.
Treatment Plan:  Post-operative care in the Surgical Intensive Care Unit (SICU).  Pain management with PCA morphine.  Intravenous antibiotics (Cefazolin) for prophylaxis.  NG tube to remain in place.


**[October 28, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: SICU Physician
Reason for Visit: Post-operative monitoring.
Interventions:  Vital signs monitoring, assessment of bowel sounds, IV fluid management.
Findings/Results:  Patient stable, tolerating PO fluids well.  Bowel sounds present.  NG tube removed.
Treatment Plan:  Transfer to general surgical floor.  Continue pain management as needed.  Advance diet as tolerated.


**[October 30, 2023, 15:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Post-operative follow-up.
Interventions:  Wound assessment, review of labs.
Findings/Results:  Surgical wound healing well.  WBC count normalized.  Pathology report revealed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon.
Treatment Plan:  Discharge planning initiated.  Follow-up appointment with oncology scheduled for next week.


**[November 2, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Discussion of cancer diagnosis and treatment plan.
Interventions:  Review of pathology report, discussion of treatment options.
Findings/Results:  Confirmed Stage II colon cancer.
Treatment Plan:  Recommendation for adjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX regimen.  Further staging investigations including CT chest/abdomen/pelvis.


**[November 10, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician
Reason for Visit:  Fever, chills, and increased WBC.
Interventions:  Blood cultures, urine culture, chest X-ray.
Findings/Results:  Blood cultures positive for *E. coli*. Chest X-ray showed a left lower lobe pneumonia.
Treatment Plan:  Initiated IV antibiotics (Piperacillin/tazobactam).


**[November 15, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician
Reason for Visit:  Discharge planning.
Interventions:  Review of progress, education on medication regimen, wound care.
Findings/Results:  Resolution of infection.  Patient clinically stable.
Treatment Plan: Discharge to home with instructions on wound care and medication regimen.


**3. Key Events During Hospitalization**

* Sigmoid colectomy performed on October 27, 2023, without major complications.
* Pathology confirmed Stage II colon cancer.
* Development of postoperative *E. coli* infection requiring IV antibiotics.
* Anemia and dehydration initially present, requiring fluid resuscitation.

**4. Ongoing Management and Care**

Mr. Miller received intravenous fluids, pain management (morphine), antibiotics (Cefazolin, then Piperacillin/tazobactam), and nutritional support during his hospital stay.  He underwent a sigmoid colectomy and received post-operative care, including wound care and monitoring for complications.  He was also seen by an oncologist for discussion of his cancer diagnosis and treatment planning.

**5. Discharge Summary**

Discharge Medications:
* Oxaliplatin, Leucovorin, 5-fluorouracil (FOLFOX regimen) – as per oncologist’s prescription.
* Acetaminophen for pain management.
* Senna for bowel regularity.

Follow-up Instructions:
* Follow-up appointment with oncology in one week to begin chemotherapy.
* Follow-up appointment with general surgeon in two weeks for wound check.
* Contact physician if fever, increased pain, or worsening wound.

Prognosis:  Guarded.  Prognosis depends on response to chemotherapy.  Regular follow-up is crucial for monitoring disease progression and managing any potential complications.

**[November 22, 2023, 10:30]**

Provider Role: Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  First cycle of FOLFOX chemotherapy.
Interventions:  Administration of Oxaliplatin, Leucovorin, and 5-fluorouracil (FOLFOX) chemotherapy.  Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), assessment for adverse effects.
Findings/Results:  CBC showed mild leukopenia (WBC 3,500/µL), otherwise within normal limits. CMP unremarkable. Patient reported mild nausea and fatigue.  No significant allergic reactions to chemotherapy.
Treatment Plan:  Continue FOLFOX regimen as scheduled.  Prescribed Ondansetron for nausea.  Scheduled follow-up appointment next week for blood work and symptom assessment.  Instructed patient to report any significant increase in fatigue, fever, or shortness of breath.


**[November 29, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up after first cycle of FOLFOX.
Interventions:  Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), review of symptoms.
Findings/Results:  CBC showed improved WBC count (4,800/µL).  CMP unremarkable.  Patient reported that nausea was well-controlled with Ondansetron. Fatigue persists but is manageable.  No fever or shortness of breath.
Treatment Plan:  Second cycle of FOLFOX scheduled for next week.  Continue Ondansetron as needed.  Encourage increased hydration and rest.  Closely monitor for signs of neutropenia.


**[December 6, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Surgical wound check.
Interventions:  Physical examination of surgical wound site.
Findings/Results:  Surgical wound is well-healed, with minimal scarring.  No signs of infection or dehiscence.  Patient reports minimal discomfort.
Treatment Plan:  No further intervention needed at this time.  Schedule another follow-up in 4 weeks if needed.  Advised patient to continue monitoring for any signs of infection (increased pain, redness, swelling, drainage).


**[December 13, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Second cycle of FOLFOX chemotherapy and follow-up.
Interventions: Administration of Oxaliplatin, Leucovorin, and 5-fluorouracil (FOLFOX) chemotherapy. Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), assessment for adverse effects.
Findings/Results:  CBC showed mild thrombocytopenia (platelets 100,000/µL).  CMP showed mild increase in liver enzymes (AST/ALT). Patient reported increased fatigue and peripheral neuropathy (tingling in hands and feet).
Treatment Plan:  Hold the next cycle of FOLFOX pending further blood work and evaluation of liver enzymes.  Prescribed folic acid and Vitamin B12 supplements.  Referred to physical therapy for management of peripheral neuropathy. Scheduled follow up in one week for repeat blood work and symptom assessment.


**3. Key Events During Hospitalization** (Existing Note Entry updated below)

* Sigmoid colectomy performed on October 27, 2023, without major complications.
* Pathology confirmed Stage II colon cancer.
* Development of postoperative *E. coli* infection requiring IV antibiotics.
* Anemia and dehydration initially present, requiring fluid resuscitation.
* Post-operative course complicated by mild thrombocytopenia and elevated liver enzymes during second cycle of FOLFOX chemotherapy.

**4. Ongoing Management and Care** (Existing Note Entry updated below)

Mr. Miller received intravenous fluids, pain management (morphine), antibiotics (Cefazolin, then Piperacillin/tazobactam), and nutritional support during his hospital stay.  He underwent a sigmoid colectomy and received post-operative care, including wound care and monitoring for complications.  He was also seen by an oncologist for discussion of his cancer diagnosis and treatment planning. He is currently undergoing FOLFOX chemotherapy, with management of associated side effects such as nausea, fatigue, and peripheral neuropathy.

**5. Discharge Summary** (Existing Note Entry updated below)

Discharge Medications:
* Oxaliplatin, Leucovorin, 5-fluorouracil (FOLFOX regimen) – as per oncologist’s prescription (currently on hold due to thrombocytopenia and elevated liver enzymes).
* Ondansetron for nausea.
* Acetaminophen for pain management.
* Senna for bowel regularity.
* Folic Acid and Vitamin B12 supplements.

Follow-up Instructions:
* Follow-up appointment with oncology in one week for blood work and symptom assessment.
* Follow-up appointment with general surgeon as needed.
* Contact physician if fever, increased pain, or worsening wound.  Also report any significant increase in fatigue, bleeding, bruising, or shortness of breath.

Prognosis:  Guarded.  Prognosis depends on response to chemotherapy.  Regular follow-up is crucial for monitoring disease progression and managing any potential complications.  Treatment plan may need adjustment based on response and tolerance to chemotherapy.
